salient_findings: Hypoechogenic subcardial mass on the posterior gastric wall
Recurrent bleeding tumor at the same site after resection
key_facts: 48-year-old woman
7-year history of submucosal tumor below the esophagogastric junction
Presented with melena and progressive anemia
Hemoglobin level was 7.5 g/dL
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed a 70 × 50 × 55 mm hypoechogenic mass
Subcardial mass on the posterior gastric wall
Lesion was resected endoscopically by a piecemeal technique under general anesthesia
Histopathology reportedly confirmed a lipoma
Recurrent bleeding tumor at the same site six weeks after resection

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent bleeding submucosal gastric tumor with high risk of malignancy

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Initial histopathology confirmed a lipoma, but recurrence suggests possible malignant transformation

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal tumor with rapid growth and bleeding, consistent with smooth muscle tumor

shortlist.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant tumor with potential for submucosal involvement and bleeding

shortlist.label: Glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but possible cause of recurrent bleeding submucosal gastric tumor

raw.rationale: The patient's 7-year history of a submucosal tumor and its recurrence after resection, along with the presentation of melena and progressive anemia, are more indicative of a malignant tumor such as a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) rather than a benign lipoma. GISTs are known to occur in the stomach, can cause bleeding, and have a potential for recurrence.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Liposarcomas are rare in the gastrointestinal tract and the initial diagnosis of lipoma does not align with the aggressive behavior of the tumor

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: While leiomyosarcomas can occur in the stomach, the description provided does not specifically point towards smooth muscle origin

rejected.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The tumor's submucosal location and description do not typically match gastric adenocarcinoma, which usually arises from the mucosa

rejected.label: Glomus tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumors are rare and typically present with pain and bleeding, but the size and location described are less characteristic of glomus tumors

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: The initial diagnosis of lipoma is contradicted by the tumor's aggressive behavior and recurrence
